maya: Heads up — after the deploy last night I see a notable drop in prefix cache hit-rate for RAG workloads (esp. doc-heavy, long-context). Looks like affected hosts are on kernel_swap v2. sam: Can you share numbers? maya: peak @ 18:30 UTC we saw prefix_hit_rate go from ~0.68 to ~0.45 on the RAG cluster, overall token latency +12% and token compute cost up ~22%. attaching quick profiler snippets below. ben: That matches the request traces I pulled — a lot of small, unique prefix keys for doc retrieval prompts (shingled snippets) so key-cardinality shot up. ashley: Could this be the kernel selection change that prefers the quantized path for smaller seqs? lucas: Unclear — kernel_swap v2 changed kernel selection heuristics: it now picks fast quant kernels for <64 seq by default, which interacts badly with our continuous-batching shims. infra-bot: deploy #infra/runtime-kernel_swap_v2 rolled at 2026-03-16T02:12Z. sam: I profiled one host (host-77): KV cache prefetch hits dropped from 0.72 -> 0.38, eviction churn rose 3x. sample log:
```
KV_PREFETCH_STATS: prefetched=4323, hits=1641, hit_rate=0.38, evictions=1297
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8, avg_token_latency=11.4ms
```
maya: The interesting part is chat completions clusters didn't regress as badly (~5-8% hit loss). So this is workload-specific. ben: Chat prefixes tend to be short and repeatable; RAG uses longer document fingerprints and variable window boundaries -> key normalization sensitivity. ashley: Could be our prefix keying function: we included convo metadata (user_id, session_id) in some keys for structured outputs. That inflates cardinality. lucas: Agreed — I found a code path where structured-output customers opt into metadata_in_key=true. Those RAG pipelines had that enabled. sam: Actionable triage: 1) reproduce with synthetic RAG workload, 2) test kernel_swap v1 vs v2 with identical inputs, 3) run batch-window sweep (5/10/15/30ms) to see hit/latency tradeoffs, 4) check key normalization and strip session-level details. ben: I ran a quick synthetic with 10k doc prompts (shingle size 64, overlap 8). Repro is solid. With kernel_swap v1: prefetch_hit_rate=0.69, v2: 0.41. Increasing batch window to 20ms on v2 brought hit_rate to 0.56 but added 6% tail latency. ashley: So a path forward: short-term rollback possibility (v1) for RAG Dedicated pools; medium-term fix: add an adaptive prefetch policy that groups by shingle fingerprint rather than full prefix key; long-term: key normalization API change to default-exclude volatile convo metadata. maya: I like adaptive prefetch. Could we implement a lightweight splay that maps shingled doc spans into a canonical fingerprint before cache lookup? lucas: Yes — we can add a canonicalization layer: normalize whitespace, truncate to token-window buckets, strip session tags. It's cheap, CPU-wise. sam: I'll prototype a mapping that emits <doc_fingerprint>:<bucket_id> as cache key. ben: We need to be careful with structured outputs — some customers intentionally rely on metadata in responses. API default should be safe but allow opt-in for metadata_in_key. ashley: Also need to update our batching heuristics — v2's kernel selection aggressively packs small seqs which reduces per-request batching overlap for RAG. If we widen batch coalescing window for RAG routes, we get better KV reuse. lucas: Proposed immediate tasks (kanban): - canary kernel_swap v1 rollback for dedicated-rag (owner: maya) - prototype fingerprint canonicalizer (owner: sam) - batch-window sweep jobs (owner: ben) - flag to default-exclude volatile convo metadata (owner: ashley) - perf regression postmortem doc (owner: maya)
maya: I'll open the canary rollback PR and coordinate with infra. ben: I'll run the sweep overnight and post summary. sam: Prototype will be a 2-file change: lookup canonicalizer + unit tests. Quick snippet of the canonicalizer concept:
```
def canonicalize_prefix(text, bucket_size=128):
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text).strip()
    fp = sha1(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    bucket = (len(text) // bucket_size)
    return f"{fp}:{bucket}"
```
lucas: Nice — that will collapse many near-duplicates. Add a feature-flagged rollout. ashley: For observability, add per-route prefetched_key_cardinality metric and prefetched_key_collision rate so we can see when canonicalization helps. infra-bot: ticket #INF-6213 created: "RAG prefix regression triage" assigned to maya,sam,ben. maya: Ok we'll try the canonicalizer on a canary host with v2 and batch_window=20ms. If hit_rate >0.6 and p99 latency delta <8% we'll proceed to wider rollout. sam: I'll post the canary results here tomorrow. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
